# Tool reference

Every operation Legion performs is a tool with a name, an effect, and a JSON Schema for its
arguments. The command line, MCP, HTTP, and RPC doors expose the same registry, so a tool listed
here behaves identically through every door.

Run `legion tools` on any machine to see its live registry (including any local extensions in
`tools.d/`), or `legion help <tool>` for one tool's schema.

Families (15, 75 tools total): [`agent`](#agent), [`audit`](#audit), [`config`](#config), [`device`](#device), [`exec`](#exec), [`ext`](#ext), [`fleet`](#fleet), [`fs`](#fs), [`job`](#job), [`meta`](#meta), [`power`](#power), [`proj`](#proj), [`svc`](#svc), [`sys`](#sys), [`token`](#token).

## agent

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.add` | `admin` | Register this `legion` binary as an MCP server named `legion` with an AI coding agent using the agent's own CLI command, never by editing its configuration files directly. |
| `agent.list` | `admin` | Check each known AI coding agent (claude, codex, antigravity, opencode) to see whether its CLI is on PATH and whether an MCP server named `legion` is registered via its own `mcp list` command. |
| `agent.remove` | `admin` | Remove the `legion` MCP server registration from an AI coding agent using the agent's own CLI command, never by editing its configuration files directly. |

### `agent.add`

Effect: `admin`

Register this `legion` binary as an MCP server named `legion` with an AI coding agent using the agent's own CLI command, never by editing its configuration files directly. `compact` defaults to true because every registered tool schema costs the agent context on every conversation; pass `compact=false` to expose every tool individually. A named, limited principal from policy.toml (such as `agent:claude` with the `editor` or `observer` role) is safer than `owner` because it narrows what the agent may do and identifies its calls in the audit log; registering as `owner` requires `allow_owner=true`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | `string` | yes | - | Which AI coding agent to register Legion with (`claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`, `opencode`). `claude`: Claude Code (`claude`). `codex`: OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex`). `antigravity`: Antigravity CLI (`agy`). `opencode`: OpenCode (`opencode`). Allowed values: `claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`, `opencode`. |
| `as` | `string` | yes | - | Principal every MCP call from this agent acts as. Must be named in policy.toml, or `owner` with `allow_owner=true`. Prefer a named, limited principal so the agent is confined by its role and clearly identified in the audit log. |
| `compact` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Pass `--compact` to `legion mcp` (exposes four meta-tools instead of one per registered tool). Defaults to true because every registered tool schema costs context on every conversation. |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | Scope for agents that support one (`local`, `user`, or `project` for `claude`, default `user`; `global`/`user` or `project`/`local` for `opencode`, default `global`). |
| `allow_owner` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Allow registering the agent as `owner`, which grants unrestricted access. Off unless true. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Return the exact registration command without running it. |

### `agent.list`

Effect: `admin`

Check each known AI coding agent (claude, codex, antigravity, opencode) to see whether its CLI is on PATH and whether an MCP server named `legion` is registered via its own `mcp list` command.

Takes no arguments.

### `agent.remove`

Effect: `admin`

Remove the `legion` MCP server registration from an AI coding agent using the agent's own CLI command, never by editing its configuration files directly.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | `string` | yes | - | Which AI coding agent to remove Legion from (`claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`, `opencode`). `claude`: Claude Code (`claude`). `codex`: OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex`). `antigravity`: Antigravity CLI (`agy`). `opencode`: OpenCode (`opencode`). Allowed values: `claude`, `codex`, `antigravity`, `opencode`. |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | Scope for `claude` (`local`, `user`, or `project`; defaults to `user`). |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Return the exact removal command without running it. |

## audit

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.tail` | `read` | Show the last calls this node recorded in its audit log, oldest first: when, by whom, through which door, which tool, how it ended and how long it took, with file contents and secrets in the arguments replaced by their size. |

### `audit.tail`

Effect: `read`

Show the last calls this node recorded in its audit log, oldest first: when, by whom, through which door, which tool, how it ended and how long it took, with file contents and secrets in the arguments replaced by their size. Filters narrow it to a principal, a tool glob or an outcome.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | `20` | How many entries to return, from 1 to 1000. Range: 1 to 1000. |
| `principal` | `string` | no | - | Only calls that acted as this principal, such as `agent:claude`. |
| `tool` | `string` | no | - | Only calls to tools this glob matches, such as `fs.*`. |
| `outcome` | `string` | no | - | Only calls that ended this way: `ok`, or an error code such as `denied`. |

## config

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config.list` | `admin` | List the shared configuration documents present on this node (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, and files in tools.d/). |
| `config.read` | `admin` | Read one shared configuration document (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, or tools.d/<name>.toml) and its BLAKE3 content hash. |
| `config.write` | `admin` | Validate and atomically replace one shared configuration document (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, or tools.d/<name>.toml), keeping the previous version as a backup in the state directory and recording the hash before and after in the audit log. |

### `config.list`

Effect: `admin`

List the shared configuration documents present on this node (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, and files in tools.d/). Machine-local files (node.toml, tokens.toml) are never included.

Takes no arguments.

### `config.read`

Effect: `admin`

Read one shared configuration document (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, or tools.d/<name>.toml) and its BLAKE3 content hash. Refuses machine-local files such as node.toml and tokens.toml.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | `string` | yes | - | Shared document name: `fleet.toml`, `policy.toml`, `projects.toml`, or `tools.d/<name>.toml`. |

### `config.write`

Effect: `admin`

Validate and atomically replace one shared configuration document (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, or tools.d/<name>.toml), keeping the previous version as a backup in the state directory and recording the hash before and after in the audit log. Writing policy.toml changes who may do what on this machine. Refuses invalid documents before replacing anything, refuses mismatched expect_hash or expect_absent (when a file already exists) with conflict, and refuses machine-local files such as node.toml and tokens.toml.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | `string` | yes | - | Shared document name: `fleet.toml`, `policy.toml`, `projects.toml`, or `tools.d/<name>.toml`. |
| `content` | `string` | yes | - | Full UTF-8 TOML text to validate and write atomically. |
| `expect_hash` | `string` | no | - | Expected BLAKE3 hash (`blake3:<hex>`) of the existing file; fails with `conflict` if different. |
| `expect_absent` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Require that the document does not currently exist; fails with `conflict` if already present. |

## device

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device.invite` | `admin` | Create a single-use pairing invite for a remote device to connect over SSH, pinned to one principal that policy.toml names and the caller could act as itself. |
| `device.list` | `admin` | List paired devices and pending pairing invites for principals the caller could act as, reading authorized_keys as the source of truth joined with recorded metadata, and sweeping any expired or used invites. |
| `device.remove` | `admin` | Remove a paired device by name or revoke a pending pairing invite by id for a principal the caller could act as, deleting its authorized_keys line(s) and recorded metadata. |

### `device.invite`

Effect: `admin`

Create a single-use pairing invite for a remote device to connect over SSH, pinned to one principal that policy.toml names and the caller could act as itself. Appends a temporary key with sshd's expiry-time and a forced enrolment command to authorized_keys, and returns the invite text once (never logged or stored). Inviting for a principal with the owner role requires an owner caller and allow_owner=true.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | `string` | yes | - | The principal the paired device will act as. Must be named in policy.toml (or have the owner role with allow_owner=true) and be one the caller could act as. |
| `valid_minutes` | `integer` | no | `15` | Minutes until the invite expires, from 1 to 1440 (default 15). Range: 1 to 1440. |
| `host` | `array of string` | no | - | Host name or IP address (a single string or a list of strings) to put in the invite, overriding automatic Tailscale/hostname detection. |
| `port` | `integer` | no | `22` | SSH port on this machine (default 22). Range: 1 to 65535. |
| `user` | `string` | no | - | OS account name on this machine (defaults to the account legion runs as). |
| `allow_owner` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Allow inviting a device as a principal with the owner role, which may do everything the account can. Off unless given as true. |

### `device.list`

Effect: `admin`

List paired devices and pending pairing invites for principals the caller could act as, reading authorized_keys as the source of truth joined with recorded metadata, and sweeping any expired or used invites.

Takes no arguments.

### `device.remove`

Effect: `admin`

Remove a paired device by name or revoke a pending pairing invite by id for a principal the caller could act as, deleting its authorized_keys line(s) and recorded metadata.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | no | - | Paired device name to remove, as `device.list` shows it. Give `name` or `id`, not both. |
| `id` | `string` | no | - | Pending invite id to revoke, as `device.list` shows it. Give `name` or `id`, not both. |

## exec

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exec.run` | `exec` | Run a command that finishes and return its exit code and output. |

### `exec.run`

Effect: `exec`

Run a command that finishes and return its exit code and output. Give `argv` to run a program with exactly these arguments, or `cmd` to hand one line to the platform shell (sh on Linux and macOS, PowerShell on Windows). The command is stopped, with everything it started, when `timeout_s` passes or the call is cancelled; a non-zero exit or a timeout is reported in the result, not as an error. Output is streamed as stdout and stderr events while it runs and capped at `max_output` bytes per stream, keeping the start and the end. The command gets legion's environment (except legion's own LEGION_* settings) plus `env`, as a command typed by the account would. Not for anything meant to keep running, such as a server or a watcher: that belongs to job.start. A command can do anything the account can, so a role's `paths` decide only the directory it starts in (the first of them when `cwd` is absent), and a role that must stay confined should not be given exec.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cmd` | `string` | no | - | A command line handed whole to the platform shell: sh on Linux and macOS, PowerShell on Windows. Give this or `argv`, not both. |
| `argv` | `array of string` | no | - | The program and its arguments, run exactly as given with no shell in between. Give this or `cmd`, not both. |
| `cwd` | `string` | no | - | The absolute directory to run in. When absent: the first of the role's `paths` if it has any, otherwise legion's own. |
| `env` | `object` | no | - | Environment variables to set on top of legion's own. |
| `stdin` | `string` | no | - | Text written to the command's standard input, which is then closed. Without it the command reads end of input at once. |
| `timeout_s` | `number` | no | - | Seconds before the command is stopped, up to 3600; 120 when absent. |
| `max_output` | `integer` | no | - | Bytes of output kept per stream, up to 1048576; 65536 when absent. Beyond it the start and the end are kept and the middle is replaced by a note of how much was left out. Minimum: 0. |

## ext

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ext.define` | `admin` | Define or replace an extension tool in tools.d/<name>.toml. |
| `ext.list` | `read` | List extension tools loaded from tools.d/ with each tool's declared effect and execution mode (`run` directly or `cmd` through the shell), along with any broken files that failed to parse or validate. |
| `ext.remove` | `admin` | Remove an extension tool's definition file from tools.d/. |
| `ext.show` | `read` | Show the full stored definition of one extension tool from tools.d/. |

### `ext.define`

Effect: `admin`

Define or replace an extension tool in tools.d/<name>.toml. A tool declared `read` is callable by every role that may read, whatever its command does, so declare each tool's effect honestly. Give `run` (exact argv) or `cmd` (platform shell line), never both; caller arguments are never spliced into the command and arrive only as `LEGION_ARG_<NAME>` environment variables (upper-cased) and as one JSON object on stdin, alongside `LEGION_TOOL`, `LEGION_PRINCIPAL` and `LEGION_NODE`. Refuses to overwrite an existing extension unless `replace` is true, and refuses built-in names or reserved Legion families.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Tool name as `family.verb` in lower case (e.g. `gpu.free`). Cannot be a built-in tool or a reserved Legion family. |
| `description` | `string` | yes | - | What the tool does, shown in tool listings and to AI agents. |
| `effect` | `string` | yes | - | What the tool can do to the machine; policy rules and MCP annotations use this effect. `read`: Looks without changing anything. `write`: Changes files or configuration. `exec`: Runs a program. `destroy`: Removes or overwrites something that cannot be had back. `power`: Sleeps, restarts or powers off a machine. `admin`: Changes Legion itself. Allowed values: `read`, `write`, `exec`, `destroy`, `power`, `admin`. |
| `run` | `array of string` | no | - | Exact program and arguments to run with no shell in between. Give this or `cmd`, not both. |
| `cmd` | `string` | no | - | Command line handed to the platform shell (sh on Linux and macOS, PowerShell on Windows). Give this or `run`, not both. |
| `params` | `object` | no | - | Parameters the tool accepts, keyed by parameter name. Values arrive as `LEGION_ARG_<NAME>` environment variables and as JSON on stdin. |
| `timeout_s` | `number` | no | - | Seconds before the command is stopped, up to 3600; 60 when absent. |
| `cwd` | `string` | no | - | Optional working directory for the command (absolute path or starting with `~`). |
| `replace` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Overwrite an existing extension with the same name. Off unless given as true. |

### `ext.list`

Effect: `read`

List extension tools loaded from tools.d/ with each tool's declared effect and execution mode (`run` directly or `cmd` through the shell), along with any broken files that failed to parse or validate.

Takes no arguments.

### `ext.remove`

Effect: `admin`

Remove an extension tool's definition file from tools.d/.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | The extension tool's name, as ext.list shows it. |

### `ext.show`

Effect: `read`

Show the full stored definition of one extension tool from tools.d/.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | The extension tool's name, as ext.list shows it. |

## fleet

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fleet.add` | `admin` | Add or replace a machine entry in fleet.toml atomically while preserving comments and unrelated entries. |
| `fleet.discover` | `read` | Discover peer machines from `tailscale status --json` using their MagicDNS names. |
| `fleet.install` | `admin` | Install or upgrade the legion binary on a machine in fleet.toml using only ssh and scp. |

| `fleet.sync` | `admin` | Compare, push, or pull shared configuration documents (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, and tools.d/*.toml) across machines in fleet.toml using per-peer BLAKE3 sync sidecars to detect conflicts. |

### `fleet.add`

Effect: `admin`

Add or replace a machine entry in fleet.toml atomically while preserving comments and unrelated entries.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Machine name (lower-case letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or digit). |
| `ssh` | `string` | no | - | SSH target accepted by the system ssh client. Give one of `ssh`, `command`, `systems` or `via`. |
| `command` | `array of string` | no | - | Exact argv to start `legion rpc`. Give one of `ssh`, `command`, `systems` or `via`. |
| `systems` | `array of object` | no | - | Multiple bootable systems for a dual-boot machine. Give one of `ssh`, `command`, `systems` or `via`. |
| `via` | `string` | no | - | Relay machine in `fleet.toml` through which calls to this machine are forwarded. Give one of `ssh`, `command`, `systems` or `via`. |
| `program` | `string` | no | - | Remote `legion` binary name or path when it is not found the default way. |
| `os` | `string` | no | - | Operating system hint (`"unix"` or `"windows"`). `unix`: Linux, macOS, or another POSIX-like host reached through `sh -c`. `windows`: Windows host where `legion` is on `PATH`. Allowed values: `unix`, `windows`. |
| `mac` | `string` | no | - | Hardware MAC address for waking the machine, such as `"02:00:00:00:00:01"`. |
| `wake_via` | `array of string` | no | - | Helper machines that can wake this machine. |

### `fleet.discover`

Effect: `read`

Discover peer machines from `tailscale status --json` using their MagicDNS names. Only peers belonging to this node's own Tailscale user (`Self.UserID`) are listed, and shared-in nodes (`ShareeNode`) are skipped so calls and `--on all` never reach machines owned by someone else. Tagged nodes are marked `addable: false` and skipped by `add: true` (add them explicitly with `fleet.add`). Pass `add: true` (requires admin permission) to add unlisted addable peers to fleet.toml.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `add` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Add every addable discovered machine (same Tailscale user, not shared in, not tagged) that is not already listed in fleet.toml. Requires admin permission. |

### `fleet.install`

Effect: `admin`

Install or upgrade the legion binary on a machine in fleet.toml using only ssh and scp. Detects the remote OS and architecture, verifies the offline Ed25519 signature (SHA256SUMS.sig) against the compiled-in release key and checks SHA-256 (for both downloaded and cached releases, with no skip flag; passing `from=<local file>` is the only way to install an unsigned binary, where the admin naming the file vouches for it), copies it atomically into place, and opens a normal session to verify the installed version.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | `string` | yes | - | Name of the machine in `fleet.toml` to install or upgrade `legion` on. |
| `version` | `string` | no | - | Release version to install (for example `0.2.0` or `legion-v0.2.0`). Defaults to the latest published `legion-v*` release. Cannot be combined with `from`. |
| `from` | `string` | no | - | Local path on this node to a `legion` binary already built for the target machine. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Probe the remote machine and report what would be copied where without modifying it. |
| `allow_downgrade` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Permit installing a version older than the machine's current version or recorded version floor. |

### `fleet.list`

Effect: `read`

List the machines configured in fleet.toml, their systems and transport targets, without making network connections.

Takes no arguments.

### `fleet.ping`

Effect: `read`

Check whether machines in fleet.toml answer hello, concurrently, reporting their node name, system, version, platform and latency.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machines` | `array of string` | no | - | Machine names to probe; every machine in fleet.toml when absent. |
| `timeout_s` | `number` | no | - | Seconds to wait per machine, up to 60; 8 when absent. |

### `fleet.remove`

Effect: `admin`

Remove a machine entry from fleet.toml atomically while preserving comments and unrelated entries.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Name of the machine to remove from fleet.toml. |

### `fleet.sync`

Effect: `admin`

Compare, push, or pull shared configuration documents (fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, and tools.d/*.toml) across machines in fleet.toml using per-peer BLAKE3 sync sidecars to detect conflicts. In status mode, reports same, changed_here, changed_there, both, only_here, or only_there. Removal of a tools.d file is never propagated: push never deletes remote files, pull never deletes local files, and status reports files present on only one side as only_here or only_there. Syncing policy.toml is powerful because it changes who may do what on the receiving machine; every replacement is strictly validated by the receiver before installing, backed up, and recorded in the audit log with its hash before and after. Never syncs node.toml or tokens.toml.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machines` | `array of string` | no | - | Machines to sync with; defaults to all machines in fleet.toml other than this node. |
| `documents` | `array of string` | no | - | Shared documents to sync; defaults to fleet.toml, policy.toml, projects.toml, and any tools.d/*.toml files. |
| `direction` | `string` | no | `"status"` | `status` (default, compares hashes only), `push` (local -> remote), or `pull` (remote -> local). `status`: Compare BLAKE3 hashes without writing anything. `push`: Send local shared documents to remote machines when they have not diverged. `pull`: Fetch shared documents from one remote machine when local copies have not diverged. Allowed values: `status`, `push`, `pull`. |
| `from` | `string` | no | - | Source machine to pull from when `direction` is `pull`. |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Overwrite conflicts without failing (the receiver still validates every document strictly). |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Report what would happen without modifying any configuration, backup, or sidecar files. |

## fs

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fs.copy` | `write` | Copy a file, symbolic link or directory tree without following symbolic links out of the tree. |
| `fs.edit` | `write` | Replace an exact string in a UTF-8 text file atomically while preserving line endings and permissions, with optional expect_hash conflict checking. |
| `fs.find` | `read` | Find files and directories under a path matching optional glob, kind and depth filters, respecting .gitignore and skipping hidden entries by default. |
| `fs.grep` | `read` | Search text files for a regular expression with optional glob filter and context lines, skipping binary files and truncating very long lines. |
| `fs.hash` | `read` | Stream a file and return its size and BLAKE3 digest as blake3:<hex>. |
| `fs.list` | `read` | List entries in a directory up to a bounded depth and count, directories first then by name, reporting symbolic links without following them. |
| `fs.manifest` | `read` | List a directory tree (or one file) the way fs.transfer compares it: each entry's relative path, kind, size, modification time, mode, link target and, with checksum, its BLAKE3 hash. |
| `fs.mkdir` | `write` | Create a directory and, by default, any missing parent directories. |
| `fs.move` | `write` | Move or rename a file, symbolic link or directory, falling back to copy-then-remove across file systems. |
| `fs.read` | `read` | Read up to 1 MiB of a file from an offset as UTF-8 or base64, returning the whole-file BLAKE3 hash when the entire file fit in this reply. |
| `fs.remove` | `destroy` | Remove a file, symbolic link or directory (with optional recursive and dry_run modes), refusing roots, the home directory and Legion's own directories. |
| `fs.stat` | `read` | Return metadata for a path (kind, size, modification time, Unix mode, readonly flag, and symbolic link target) without following a symbolic link. |
| `fs.transfer` | `write` | Copy a file or a directory tree between machines, or within one. |
| `fs.write` | `write` | Write UTF-8 text or base64 bytes to a file atomically, supporting overwrite, create-only and append modes, optional expect_hash conflict checks, parent creation and Unix mode. |

Effect: `write`

Copy a file, symbolic link or directory tree without following symbolic links out of the tree.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### `fs.edit`

Effect: `write`

Replace an exact string in a UTF-8 text file atomically while preserving line endings and permissions, with optional expect_hash conflict checking.
