| `expect_hash` | `string` | no | - | Require the current file's BLAKE3 hash (`blake3:<hex>`) to match before editing. |

### `fs.find`

Effect: `read`

Find files and directories under a path matching optional glob, kind and depth filters, respecting .gitignore and skipping hidden entries by default.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | Root directory to search (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `glob` | `string` | no | - | Optional glob pattern (for example `"**/*.rs"` or `"*.toml"`). |
| `kind` | `string` | no | - | Optional entry kind filter (`file`, `dir`, `symlink` or `other`). `file`: A regular file. `dir`: A directory. `symlink`: A symbolic link. `other`: Something else, such as a named pipe, socket or device node. Allowed values: `file`, `dir`, `symlink`, `other`. |
| `max_depth` | `integer` | no | - | Maximum directory depth to descend (1 means direct children only). Minimum: 1. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | `200` | Maximum number of matches to return, from 1 to 5000. Range: 1 to 5000. |
| `ignore` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Respect `.gitignore` / `.ignore` rules and skip hidden files. |
| `cross_filesystems` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Descend into directories mounted from other file systems (false stays on one file system). |

### `fs.grep`

Effect: `read`

Search text files for a regular expression with optional glob filter and context lines, skipping binary files and truncating very long lines.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | File or directory to search (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `pattern` | `string` | yes | - | Regular expression pattern to search for. |
| `glob` | `string` | no | - | Optional glob filter restricting which files are searched (for example `"**/*.rs"`). |
| `ignore_case` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Match without distinguishing ASCII/Unicode letter case. |
| `context` | `integer` | no | `0` | Number of surrounding lines to include before and after each match, from 0 to 5. Range: 0 to 5. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | `100` | Maximum number of matches to return, from 1 to 1000. Range: 1 to 1000. |
| `ignore` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Respect `.gitignore` / `.ignore` rules and skip hidden files when searching a directory. |
| `cross_filesystems` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Descend into directories mounted from other file systems (false stays on one file system). |

### `fs.hash`

Effect: `read`

Stream a file and return its size and BLAKE3 digest as blake3:<hex>.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | File to hash (absolute or starting with `~`). |

### `fs.list`

Effect: `read`

List entries in a directory up to a bounded depth and count, directories first then by name, reporting symbolic links without following them.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | Directory to list (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `depth` | `integer` | no | `1` | How many directory levels to descend, from 1 to 8. Range: 1 to 8. |
| `hidden` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Include hidden files and directories (dotfiles, and Windows hidden entries). |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | `500` | Maximum number of entries to return, from 1 to 5000. Range: 1 to 5000. |

### `fs.manifest`

Effect: `read`

List a directory tree (or one file) the way fs.transfer compares it: each entry's relative path, kind, size, modification time, mode, link target and, with checksum, its BLAKE3 hash. Bounded by limit.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | Directory or file to list (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `checksum` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Hash every regular file with BLAKE3, which reads all of them. |
| `exclude` | `array of string` | no | `[]` | Globs of paths to leave out, relative to `path`; a trailing `/` matches directories only. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | `1000` | Most entries to return, from 1 to 10000. Range: 1 to 10000. |

### `fs.mkdir`

Effect: `write`

Create a directory and, by default, any missing parent directories.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | Directory to create (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `parents` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Create missing parent directories and succeed if the directory already exists. |

### `fs.move`

Effect: `write`

Move or rename a file, symbolic link or directory, falling back to copy-then-remove across file systems.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `string` | yes | - | Existing path to move (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `to` | `string` | yes | - | Destination path (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `overwrite` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Replace an existing file, symbolic link or empty directory at `to`. |

### `fs.read`

Effect: `read`

Read up to 1 MiB of a file from an offset as UTF-8 or base64, returning the whole-file BLAKE3 hash when the entire file fit in this reply.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | File to read (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `offset` | `integer` | no | `0` | Byte offset to start reading from. Minimum: 0. |
| `length` | `integer` | no | `1048576` | Maximum number of bytes to read, up to 1 MiB (1048576). Range: 0 to 1048576. |
| `encoding` | `string` | no | - | Output encoding (`utf8` or `base64`); omitted selects `utf8` when valid and `base64` otherwise. `utf8`: UTF-8 text. `base64`: Standard base64-encoded bytes. Allowed values: `utf8`, `base64`. |

### `fs.remove`

Effect: `destroy`

Remove a file, symbolic link or directory (with optional recursive and dry_run modes), refusing roots, the home directory and Legion's own directories.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | Path to remove (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `recursive` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Remove a directory and everything inside it. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Report what would be removed without changing the file system. |

### `fs.stat`

Effect: `read`

Return metadata for a path (kind, size, modification time, Unix mode, readonly flag, and symbolic link target) without following a symbolic link.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | Path to inspect (absolute or starting with `~`). |

### `fs.transfer`

Effect: `write`

Copy a file or a directory tree between machines, or within one. Each of from and to is machine:/path or a path on this node; to names the destination itself, except that a file sent to an existing directory (or to a path ending in /) lands inside it under its own name. A file resumes where an interrupted transfer stopped and is renamed into place only once its BLAKE3 hash matches. A tree sends only what differs (size and modification time, or hash with checksum), so a second run sends nothing; delete removes what the source no longer has, exclude leaves paths out at both ends, and dry_run reports what would be sent and deleted without changing anything.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `string` | yes | - | What to send: `machine:/path`, or a path on this node (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `to` | `string` | yes | - | Where it goes, in the same form. It names the destination itself; a file sent to an existing directory lands inside it. |
| `delete` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Remove from the destination tree what the source no longer has. |
| `checksum` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Compare files by BLAKE3 hash instead of size and modification time, which reads them all. |
| `exclude` | `array of string` | no | `[]` | Globs of paths to leave out at both ends, relative to the tree; a trailing `/` matches directories only. What is left out at the destination is never deleted. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | List and plan, and report what would be sent and deleted, without changing anything. |

### `fs.write`

Effect: `write`

Write UTF-8 text or base64 bytes to a file atomically, supporting overwrite, create-only and append modes, optional expect_hash conflict checks, parent creation and Unix mode.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | yes | - | File to write (absolute or starting with `~`). |
| `content` | `string` | yes | - | Content to write, as UTF-8 text or standard base64 according to `encoding`. |
| `encoding` | `string` | no | `"utf8"` | Encoding of `content` (`utf8` or `base64`, default `utf8`). `utf8`: UTF-8 text. `base64`: Standard base64-encoded bytes. Allowed values: `utf8`, `base64`. |
| `mode` | `string` | no | - | Write mode (`overwrite`, `create` or `append`, default `overwrite`). `overwrite`: Create the file or atomically replace its contents. `create`: Create a new file and fail with `exists` if anything is already at the path. `append`: Append to an existing file in OS append mode or create it if missing. Allowed values: `overwrite`, `create`, `append`. |
| `expect_hash` | `string` | no | - | Require the existing file's BLAKE3 hash (`blake3:<hex>`) to match before writing. |
| `parents` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Create missing parent directories before writing. |
| `unix_mode` | `string` | no | - | Unix permissions as an octal string, such as `"0600"` or `"0644"`. Ignored on Windows. |

## job

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `job.cancel` | `exec` | Stop a running background job and its entire process tree. |
| `job.list` | `read` | List background jobs recorded on this node, newest first, with their id, name, current derived state, timestamps, exit code, and command summary. |
| `job.logs` | `read` | Read captured stdout and stderr from a background job without loading the whole log into memory. |
| `job.start` | `exec` | Start a command as a detached background job that outlives this call, this legion process, and any ssh session. |
| `job.status` | `read` | Inspect one background job's full record (without environment values), current derived state, exit code or signal, duration, output size, and failure or interruption detail without modifying anything on disk. |
| `job.wait` | `read` | Wait until a background job is no longer starting or running and return the same status object as `job.status`, plus `timed_out`. |

### `job.cancel`

Effect: `exec`

Stop a running background job and its entire process tree. Asks the job supervisor to terminate the command cleanly and escalates to stopping the detached process group or systemd scope if it does not finish within a short grace period; set `force: true` to stop the detached handle immediately. Returns only once the job is gone or reports any surviving process ids. Any principal with the exec effect can cancel any job on this node. Cancelling a job that already finished is not an error and returns its final state.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | - | The job identifier returned by `job.start` or `job.list`. |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Skip waiting for the supervisor to cancel cooperatively and terminate the detached process tree or systemd scope immediately. |

### `job.list`

Effect: `read`

List background jobs recorded on this node, newest first, with their id, name, current derived state, timestamps, exit code, and command summary. Filter by `state` to find running, failed, or interrupted jobs. Any principal with the read effect sees every job's command and output on this node. Reading never modifies job files.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `string` | no | - | Keep only jobs currently in this derived state. `starting`: The job record is written and the detached supervisor is starting up. `running`: The supervisor holds the job's kernel lock and is running the command. `succeeded`: The command exited with code 0. `failed`: The command exited with a non-zero code, ended on a signal, or failed to start. `cancelled`: The job was stopped via `job.cancel`. `interrupted`: No exit record exists and the supervisor's lock is free (the supervisor died or the machine rebooted). Allowed values: `starting`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | - | Maximum number of jobs to return, 1 to 500; 50 when absent. Range: 1 to 500. |

### `job.logs`

Effect: `read`

Read captured stdout and stderr from a background job without loading the whole log into memory. Stdout and stderr are merged into one log: each stream stays in its own order and lines (up to 64 KiB) are written whole under one lock so the two streams never split a line mid-way, while relative order between stdout and stderr is unspecified. Pass `offset` (feeding back `next_offset` from each reply) to stream new output incrementally while the job runs, or omit `offset` to read the last `tail` lines (default 100, max 5000). Replies are capped at `limit` bytes (default 65536, max 1048576), never split a UTF-8 character, and replace invalid UTF-8 bytes. Large logs rotate once into `output.log.1` and are read across both segments transparently; `output_dropped` and `dropped_bytes` report when earlier output was discarded by rotation. Any principal with the read effect sees every job's command and output on this node.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | - | The job identifier returned by `job.start` or `job.list`. |
| `offset` | `integer` | no | - | Byte offset to read forward from (feed back `next_offset` to poll incrementally). Omit to read the last `tail` lines instead. Minimum: 0. |
| `tail` | `integer` | no | - | Number of trailing lines to read when `offset` is omitted (1 to 5000; 100 by default). Range: 1 to 5000. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | - | Maximum bytes to return in one reply (1 to 1048576; 65536 by default). Range: 1 to 1048576. |

### `job.start`

Effect: `exec`

Start a command as a detached background job that outlives this call, this legion process, and any ssh session. Give `argv` to run a program with exact arguments or `cmd` for the platform shell (sh on Linux and macOS, PowerShell on Windows). Returns as soon as the job supervisor holds its lock; afterwards poll `job.logs` with `next_offset` to read output as it arrives, call `job.wait` to wait for completion, or inspect `job.status`. Pass `key` to make retries after a dropped connection idempotent: a key matches an active job or one whose supervisor took the lock and ran (succeeded, failed, cancelled, or interrupted mid-run); a failed start whose supervisor never took the lock does not match and is replaced. Set `exclusive: true` when the job should mark this machine busy.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cmd` | `string` | no | - | A command line handed whole to the platform shell: sh on Linux and macOS, PowerShell on Windows. Give this or `argv`, not both. |
| `argv` | `array of string` | no | - | The program and its arguments, run exactly as given with no shell in between. Give this or `cmd`, not both. |
| `cwd` | `string` | no | - | The absolute directory to run in (accepts `~`); legion's own when absent. |
| `env` | `object` | no | - | Environment variables to set on top of legion's own. Values are stored in a private file and never included in job records or replies. |
| `name` | `string` | no | - | Short human-readable name for the job; defaults to the command's program name. |
| `key` | `string` | no | - | Caller-chosen idempotency key. Matches an active job or one whose supervisor took the lock and ran (succeeded, failed, cancelled, or interrupted mid-run): re-calling with the same key and identical command, `cwd`, and environment variable names returns that job instead of starting a second one, while differing arguments fail with `conflict`. A failed start whose supervisor never took the lock does not match and is replaced. |
| `exclusive` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Mark this machine busy while the job runs (blocks unattended `power.*` operations). |

### `job.status`

Effect: `read`

Inspect one background job's full record (without environment values), current derived state, exit code or signal, duration, output size, and failure or interruption detail without modifying anything on disk. Pass an `id` from `job.start` or `job.list`; use `job.logs` to read output or `job.wait` to wait until it finishes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | - | The job identifier returned by `job.start` or `job.list`. |

### `job.wait`

Effect: `read`

Wait until a background job is no longer starting or running and return the same status object as `job.status`, plus `timed_out`. Returns as soon as the job reaches a terminal state, or returns with `timed_out: true` when `timeout_s` elapses (default 60, max 3600). Stops waiting immediately if this call is cancelled. Use this after `job.start` instead of polling `job.status` in a tight loop.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | - | The job identifier returned by `job.start` or `job.list`. |
| `timeout_s` | `number` | no | - | Seconds to wait before returning with `timed_out: true` (up to 3600; 60 when absent). |

## meta

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta.doctor` | `read` | Check that this node is healthy: its configuration directory can be read, its state directory exists and can be written to, every configuration file parses, the executable directory and ssh are on PATH, Linux systemd lingering is enabled, non-owner roles that allow exec are flagged as a warning, and each machine in fleet.toml is checked (unless quick=true; unreachable machines are reported as warnings while protocol or reply errors fail). |
| `meta.init` | `admin` | Create starter node.toml and policy.toml files where they do not already exist, leaving every existing file untouched so it is safe to run again. |
| `meta.update` | `admin` | Replace this node's legion binary with an offline-signed GitHub release artifact or a local binary passed with `from`. |
| `meta.version` | `read` | Say which build of legion this node runs, the protocol it speaks, and its operating system and architecture. |
| `meta.whoami` | `read` | Say who the caller is on this node: the principal and role it acts as, the door it came through, the directories file tools are confined to, and the tools it may use. |

### `meta.doctor`

Effect: `read`

Check that this node is healthy: its configuration directory can be read, its state directory exists and can be written to, every configuration file parses, the executable directory and ssh are on PATH, Linux systemd lingering is enabled, non-owner roles that allow exec are flagged as a warning, and each machine in fleet.toml is checked (unless quick=true; unreachable machines are reported as warnings while protocol or reply errors fail). Each check says what it found and, when something is wrong, what to do. It writes nothing but a probe file in the state directory, which it removes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quick` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Skip checking whether remote machines in fleet.toml answer. |

### `meta.init`

Effect: `admin`

Create starter node.toml and policy.toml files where they do not already exist, leaving every existing file untouched so it is safe to run again.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | no | - | Node name to write into node.toml when creating it; defaults to the name derived from this machine's host name. |
| `roles` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Create policy.toml with ready-made observer, editor and operator roles when missing. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Report what would be created or kept without writing any files. |

### `meta.update`

Effect: `admin`

Replace this node's legion binary with an offline-signed GitHub release artifact or a local binary passed with `from`. Release downloads require a valid Ed25519 SHA256SUMS.sig matching the public key compiled into legion (no flag can bypass it) and SHA-256 verification; passing `from=<local file>` installs an unsigned binary that the admin naming the file vouches for. Checks binary format and architecture, enforces downgrade protection unless `allow_downgrade` is set, stages and runs `--version` preflight, keeps the previous binary as `.prev` (restoring it if the replaced binary does not run), and replaces atomically. On Windows, renames the running executable aside first so it can be cleaned up on the next start.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `string` | no | - | Release version to install (for example `0.2.0` or `legion-v0.2.0`). Defaults to the highest published stable `legion-v*` semantic version. Cannot be combined with `from`. |
| `from` | `string` | no | - | Local path on this node to a `legion` binary already built for this machine. Cannot be combined with `version`. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Resolve the target release or local binary and report what would be replaced without downloading or writing. |
| `allow_downgrade` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Permit replacing with a version older than the running binary or the recorded version floor. |

### `meta.version`

Effect: `read`

Say which build of legion this node runs, the protocol it speaks, and its operating system and architecture.

Takes no arguments.

### `meta.whoami`

Effect: `read`

Say who the caller is on this node: the principal and role it acts as, the door it came through, the directories file tools are confined to, and the tools it may use.

Takes no arguments.

## power

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `power.cancel` | `power` | Call off the sleep, restart or shutdown handed over on this machine and not yet carried out: on Linux and macOS the delayed runner is stopped before it runs the command, on Windows a restart or shutdown is called off with `shutdown /a`, and a one-time firmware boot entry the restart had armed is cleared again. |
| `power.restart` | `power` | Restart this machine `delay_s` seconds (1 to 600, default 3) after this call replies, optionally into another of its systems: `into` names a boot target from node.toml ([boot.<name>]), the firmware is set to start it once and read back, and only when the setting reads back is the restart scheduled; otherwise nothing restarts. |
| `power.shutdown` | `power` | Power this machine off `delay_s` seconds (1 to 600, default 3) after this call replies. |
| `power.sleep` | `power` | Put this machine to sleep about 3 seconds after this call replies. |
| `power.status` | `read` | Report this machine's power state without changing anything: the sleep, restart or shutdown handed over and not yet carried out (`pending`, which power.cancel calls off) and how the last one ended (`last`); whether it is busy (`idle`; `busy` with the reasons, each from a busy probe or an exclusive job; or `unmonitored` when node.toml says nothing about what keeps it busy), which system of the machine this is, its boot id (which changes on every restart), the boot targets power.restart can name in `into`, and whether system actions run through sudo. |
| `power.switch` | `power` | Restart another machine, optionally into another of its systems, and confirm it came back. |
| `power.wake` | `power` | Wake a machine from fleet.toml. |
| `power.wol` | `power` | Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets from this machine for a machine named in THIS node's fleet.toml, taking its hardware address (`mac`) from there, never from the call: to the broadcast address of each connected network interface and to 255.255.255.255, port 9, three times each. |

### `power.cancel`

Effect: `power`

Call off the sleep, restart or shutdown handed over on this machine and not yet carried out: on Linux and macOS the delayed runner is stopped before it runs the command, on Windows a restart or shutdown is called off with `shutdown /a`, and a one-time firmware boot entry the restart had armed is cleared again. power.status then shows the action as `last`, cancelled, with who cancelled it. `cancelled: false` with a `detail` when nothing is pending, or when the action has already started and can no longer be stopped. Not gated on the machine being busy.

Takes no arguments.

### `power.restart`

Effect: `power`

Restart this machine `delay_s` seconds (1 to 600, default 3) after this call replies, optionally into another of its systems: `into` names a boot target from node.toml ([boot.<name>]), the firmware is set to start it once and read back, and only when the setting reads back is the restart scheduled; otherwise nothing restarts. The reply means the restart was scheduled, not that it happened, and carries the current boot id to compare with later; until it happens, power.cancel calls it off. To restart another machine and confirm which system came back, call power.switch from a different machine. Busy gate: the call fails with `busy` while a busy probe or an exclusive job says the machine is busy, or while node.toml says nothing about what keeps it busy (`unmonitored`; the error says what to write); `force: true` goes ahead anyway. Without it the state is checked again just before acting: on Linux and macOS also when the delay has passed, so a machine that became busy meanwhile is not interrupted and `last` says so; on Windows, whose own timer carries out a restart or shutdown, only when it is handed over. On Linux a logind inhibitor (an application asking not to be interrupted) also fails it with `busy`, naming who holds it; `force` does not override that, `ignore_inhibitors: true` does. One power action runs at a time: while one is pending the call fails with `conflict`. `dry_run: true` returns the exact commands without running them, and when a check would refuse the real call, what it would say (`would_refuse`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `into` | `string` | no | - | A boot target from this machine's node.toml ([boot.<name>]) to start once, such as `windows`; power.status lists them. Absent restarts into the firmware's usual choice. |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Go ahead even while the machine is busy or unmonitored. It does not override a logind inhibitor; `ignore_inhibitors` does. |
| `ignore_inhibitors` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Linux: go ahead even while a logind inhibitor (an application asking not to be interrupted, such as a running update or an unsaved document) holds the action back, through systemctl's own `-i`. It needs `[power] sudo = true`. No effect elsewhere. |
| `delay_s` | `integer` | no | - | Seconds between the reply and the restart, 1 to 600; 3 when absent. Range: 1 to 600. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Return the exact commands this call would run, without running them. |

### `power.shutdown`

Effect: `power`

Power this machine off `delay_s` seconds (1 to 600, default 3) after this call replies. The reply means the shutdown was scheduled, not that it happened; until it happens, power.cancel calls it off. Bringing the machine back takes Wake-on-LAN (power.wake from another machine) or someone at it. Busy gate: the call fails with `busy` while a busy probe or an exclusive job says the machine is busy, or while node.toml says nothing about what keeps it busy (`unmonitored`; the error says what to write); `force: true` goes ahead anyway. Without it the state is checked again just before acting: on Linux and macOS also when the delay has passed, so a machine that became busy meanwhile is not interrupted and `last` says so; on Windows, whose own timer carries out a restart or shutdown, only when it is handed over. On Linux a logind inhibitor (an application asking not to be interrupted) also fails it with `busy`, naming who holds it; `force` does not override that, `ignore_inhibitors: true` does. One power action runs at a time: while one is pending the call fails with `conflict`. `dry_run: true` returns the exact commands without running them, and when a check would refuse the real call, what it would say (`would_refuse`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Go ahead even while the machine is busy or unmonitored. It does not override a logind inhibitor; `ignore_inhibitors` does. |
| `ignore_inhibitors` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Linux: go ahead even while a logind inhibitor (an application asking not to be interrupted, such as a running update or an unsaved document) holds the action back, through systemctl's own `-i`. It needs `[power] sudo = true`. No effect elsewhere. |
| `delay_s` | `integer` | no | - | Seconds between the reply and the shutdown, 1 to 600; 3 when absent. Range: 1 to 600. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Return the exact commands this call would run, without running them. |

### `power.sleep`

Effect: `power`

Put this machine to sleep about 3 seconds after this call replies. The reply means the sleep was handed to the operating system, not that the machine is asleep. The commands in node.toml's [power] before_sleep run first, and a failure there stops the sleep. Busy gate: the call fails with `busy` while a busy probe or an exclusive job says the machine is busy, or while node.toml says nothing about what keeps it busy (`unmonitored`; the error says what to write); `force: true` goes ahead anyway. Without it the state is checked again just before acting: on Linux and macOS also when the delay has passed, so a machine that became busy meanwhile is not interrupted and `last` says so; on Windows, whose own timer carries out a restart or shutdown, only when it is handed over. On Linux a logind inhibitor (an application asking not to be interrupted) also fails it with `busy`, naming who holds it; `force` does not override that, `ignore_inhibitors: true` does. One power action runs at a time: while one is pending the call fails with `conflict`. `dry_run: true` returns the exact commands without running them, and when a check would refuse the real call, what it would say (`would_refuse`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Go ahead even while the machine is busy or unmonitored. It does not override a logind inhibitor; `ignore_inhibitors` does. |
| `ignore_inhibitors` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Linux: go ahead even while a logind inhibitor (an application asking not to be interrupted, such as a running update or an unsaved document) holds the action back, through systemctl's own `-i`. It needs `[power] sudo = true`. No effect elsewhere. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Return the exact commands this call would run, without running them. |

### `power.status`

Effect: `read`

Report this machine's power state without changing anything: the sleep, restart or shutdown handed over and not yet carried out (`pending`, which power.cancel calls off) and how the last one ended (`last`); whether it is busy (`idle`; `busy` with the reasons, each from a busy probe or an exclusive job; or `unmonitored` when node.toml says nothing about what keeps it busy), which system of the machine this is, its boot id (which changes on every restart), the boot targets power.restart can name in `into`, and whether system actions run through sudo. Busy probes run concurrently, each within its own timeout.

Takes no arguments.

### `power.switch`

Effect: `power`

Restart another machine, optionally into another of its systems, and confirm it came back. Reads the machine's boot id and system, calls power.restart on it (with `into`, a boot target in that system's node.toml, `force` and `ignore_inhibitors`; the machine's own busy gate applies, and a `busy` or `conflict` refusal comes back as is), then looks at each of the machine's systems every few seconds for up to `wait_s` seconds (0 to 900, default 180) until one answers with a different boot id. `restarted` is true only then. When `into` was given, the system that answers must be that one, or the call fails with `failed` and says which system came up instead. The connection dropping while the machine goes down is expected. With wait_s 0 the restart is only requested and `restarted` is false. `dry_run: true` returns the machine's own power.restart dry run (`would_run`, with the exact commands) and restarts nothing. Call it from a machine other than the one being restarted.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | `string` | yes | - | The machine to restart, as fleet.toml names it. |
| `into` | `string` | no | - | The system to restart into: a boot target in node.toml of the system running now, such as `windows`, which must also be the `system` the other one's node.toml names. Absent restarts into the firmware's usual choice. |
| `wait_s` | `integer` | no | - | Seconds to wait for the machine to come back, 0 to 900; 180 when absent. 0 requests the restart and returns. Range: 0 to 900. |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Restart even while the machine is busy or unmonitored. It does not override a logind inhibitor there; `ignore_inhibitors` does. |
| `ignore_inhibitors` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Restart even while a logind inhibitor holds it back (Linux, with `[power] sudo = true` there). |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Ask the machine for its power.restart dry run: the exact commands it would run, run nowhere. |

### `power.wake`

Effect: `power`

Wake a machine from fleet.toml. If it already answers, nothing is sent and `awake` is true. Otherwise each machine in its `wake_via` list is tried in order, but only one that answers right now: a helper that does not answer is skipped and never woken itself. The first that answers is asked to run power.wol for the machine, using the hardware address in the helper's own fleet.toml; with no wake_via, this machine sends the packet itself. `sent_by` names who sent it. With `wait_s` (0 to 300, default 0) the call then waits for the machine itself to answer, and `awake` is true only once it has. A packet sent is not a machine awake. `dry_run: true` chooses the sender the same way and returns where its packets would go (`would_send`) without sending any.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | `string` | yes | - | The machine to wake, as fleet.toml names it. |
| `wait_s` | `integer` | no | `0` | Seconds to wait for the machine itself to answer after the packet was sent, 0 to 300; 0 (send and return) when absent. Range: 0 to 300. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Choose the sender as a real call would, and return where its packets would go without sending any. |

### `power.wol`

Effect: `power`

Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets from this machine for a machine named in THIS node's fleet.toml, taking its hardware address (`mac`) from there, never from the call: to the broadcast address of each connected network interface and to 255.255.255.255, port 9, three times each. Wake packets only travel within the local network, so this wakes machines on the same network as this one. The reply says how many packets left; it never says the machine woke, which only the machine answering can show (power.wake waits for that). `dry_run: true` lists where the packets would go without sending any.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machine` | `string` | yes | - | The machine to wake, as this node's fleet.toml names it; its hardware address is read from there. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | `false` | List where the packets would go without sending any. |

## proj

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proj.add` | `write` | Record a project in projects.toml, or change one. |
| `proj.clone` | `exec` | Clone a project's `repo` onto this machine and record where it went. |
| `proj.discover` | `read` | Find git working trees under `root`, down to `max_depth` levels (3 unless given, at most 6), without descending into a working tree, hidden directories or dependency and build directories such as node_modules and target. |
| `proj.list` | `read` | List the projects recorded in projects.toml: each one's name, description, repo, the path it has on this machine and whether that path exists, the other machines it lives on, and the names of its tasks. |
| `proj.pull` | `exec` | Update a project on this machine from its upstream with `git pull --ff-only`, which only ever moves the branch forward. |
| `proj.remove` | `write` | Forget where a project lives on this machine, or with `everywhere: true` forget the whole project on every machine. |
| `proj.run` | `exec` | Run one of a project's tasks (see proj.list) in its directory on this machine. |
| `proj.status` | `read` | Show the git state of a project on this machine, or of every project that lives here when `project` is left out: branch, commit, upstream and how far ahead or behind it is (as of the last fetch), how many files are staged, changed, untracked or in conflict, the last commit and the stash. |

### `proj.add`

Effect: `write`

Record a project in projects.toml, or change one. With `path`, records where it lives on this machine; the directory must exist unless the project has a `repo` that proj.clone can fetch into it. Paths the project has on other machines are left as they are. `repo` and `description` are set when given. Comments and everything else in the file are kept.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | The project's name: letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, starting with a letter or digit. |
| `path` | `string` | no | - | Where it lives on this machine, absolute or starting at `~`. |
| `repo` | `string` | no | - | Where proj.clone fetches it from: any URL or path `git clone` accepts. |
| `description` | `string` | no | - | One line saying what it is. |

### `proj.clone`

Effect: `exec`

Clone a project's `repo` onto this machine and record where it went. The destination is `path` when given, else the path already recorded for this machine, else ~/projects/<name>; it must not exist or must be an empty directory. Reports git's progress as progress events and returns the commit checked out. Git never prompts: a repository that needs credentials git cannot find on its own fails instead of waiting. Git may run hooks and helpers (credential helpers, ssh) that the repository or the user configured.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `string` | yes | - | The project to clone; it must have a `repo`. |
| `path` | `string` | no | - | Where to clone it, absolute or starting at `~`; the path recorded for this machine, or ~/projects/<name>, when absent. |

### `proj.discover`

Effect: `read`

Find git working trees under `root`, down to `max_depth` levels (3 unless given, at most 6), without descending into a working tree, hidden directories or dependency and build directories such as node_modules and target. Each one found has a suggested project name, its origin remote and whether projects.toml already lists it here. With `add: true` the ones not yet listed are recorded with their paths on this machine, which needs permission to use proj.add.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `string` | yes | - | The directory to search, absolute or starting at `~`. |
| `max_depth` | `integer` | no | - | How many levels below `root` to look, 0 to 6; 3 when absent. Range: 0 to 6. |
| `add` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Record the working trees not yet listed as projects living on this machine. |

### `proj.list`

Effect: `read`

List the projects recorded in projects.toml: each one's name, description, repo, the path it has on this machine and whether that path exists, the other machines it lives on, and the names of its tasks. Every other proj tool takes a project by the name shown here. Use proj.status to see the git state of the ones that live here, and `on` to ask another machine.

Takes no arguments.

### `proj.pull`

Effect: `exec`

Update a project on this machine from its upstream with `git pull --ff-only`, which only ever moves the branch forward. When the branches have diverged or local changes are in the way, nothing changes and the call fails with `conflict`, carrying git's own explanation in the hint. Returns the commit before and after and a summary of what changed. Git may run hooks and helpers (credential helpers, ssh) that the repository or the user configured.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `string` | yes | - | The project to update. |

### `proj.remove`

Effect: `write`

Forget where a project lives on this machine, or with `everywhere: true` forget the whole project on every machine. Only projects.toml changes: no file of the project is ever deleted.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | The project's name. |
| `everywhere` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Forget the whole project on every machine, not just where it lives on this one. |

### `proj.run`

Effect: `exec`

Run one of a project's tasks (see proj.list) in its directory on this machine. `args` are added to the task's command as separate arguments, never spliced into a command line. A plain task runs to the end and returns what exec.run returns (exit code, output, whether it timed out), with output streamed as events; it is stopped after its `timeout_s`, 600 seconds unless the task says. A task marked `job = true` starts as a background job and returns its id at once: follow it with job.logs and job.wait.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `string` | yes | - | The project whose task to run. |
| `task` | `string` | yes | - | The task's name, as proj.list shows it. |
| `args` | `array of string` | no | `[]` | Arguments added after the task's command, each passed as one argument. |

### `proj.status`

Effect: `read`

Show the git state of a project on this machine, or of every project that lives here when `project` is left out: branch, commit, upstream and how far ahead or behind it is (as of the last fetch), how many files are staged, changed, untracked or in conflict, the last commit and the stash. A project whose directory is not a git repository has no `git`; one that cannot be read has an `error`, and never stops the others from being reported. Nothing is fetched and nothing is changed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `string` | no | - | The project to look at; every project that lives on this machine when absent. |

## svc

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `svc.list` | `read` | List background services managed by systemd (Linux), launchd (macOS) or the Windows Service Control Manager. |
| `svc.logs` | `read` | Read recent log lines for a background service (journald on Linux, declared plist log files on macOS, or Windows Event Log). |
| `svc.restart` | `exec` | Restart a background service and read its state back to confirm it is running. |
| `svc.start` | `exec` | Start a background service and read its state back to confirm it is running. |
| `svc.status` | `read` | Read the current state, enabled flag, PID, start time, exit code and diagnostic properties of one background service. |
| `svc.stop` | `exec` | Stop a background service and read its state back to confirm it is stopped. |

### `svc.list`

Effect: `read`

List background services managed by systemd (Linux), launchd (macOS) or the Windows Service Control Manager. `scope` selects "user" (per-user services), "system" (machine-wide services; the only scope on Windows) or "all" (default). Read-only and never escalates privileges.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | Which scope to list: `"user"`, `"system"`, or `"all"` (default `"all"`). On Windows only `"system"` exists. `user`: Only per-user services. `system`: Only machine-wide services. `all`: Both user and system services (where both exist). Allowed values: `user`, `system`, `all`. |
| `filter` | `string` | no | - | Keep only services whose name or description contains this substring (case-insensitive). |
| `state` | `string` | no | - | Keep only services in this state: `"running"`, `"stopped"` or `"failed"`. `running`: Keep only running services. `stopped`: Keep only stopped services. `failed`: Keep only failed services. Allowed values: `running`, `stopped`, `failed`. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | `100` | Maximum number of services to return, from 1 to 1000 (default 100). Range: 1 to 1000. |

### `svc.logs`

Effect: `read`

Read recent log lines for a background service (journald on Linux, declared plist log files on macOS, or Windows Event Log). When `scope` is omitted, checks "user" first and then "system" (`conflict` if in both). Read-only and never escalates privileges; long lines are cut and marked.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Service name to read logs for. |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | `"user"` or `"system"`. When omitted, checks `"user"` first and then `"system"`. `user`: Per-user service manager (`systemctl --user` on Linux, `gui/<uid>` on macOS). `system`: Machine-wide service manager (the only scope on Windows). Allowed values: `user`, `system`. |
| `lines` | `integer` | no | `100` | Maximum number of lines to return, from 1 to 2000 (default 100). Range: 1 to 2000. |
| `since` | `string` | no | - | Start of the log window: an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp (such as `2026-11-23T22:00:00Z`) or a positive duration in seconds (such as `"300"` or `300`). |

### `svc.restart`

Effect: `exec`

Restart a background service and read its state back to confirm it is running. When `scope` is omitted, checks "user" first and then "system" (`conflict` if in both). Changing a system service requires privileges: on Unix, legion never escalates unless `[svc] sudo = true` is set in node.toml (running `sudo -n`); on Windows the node must run elevated.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Service name to control. |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | `"user"` or `"system"`. When omitted, checks `"user"` first and then `"system"`. `user`: Per-user service manager (`systemctl --user` on Linux, `gui/<uid>` on macOS). `system`: Machine-wide service manager (the only scope on Windows). Allowed values: `user`, `system`. |

### `svc.start`

Effect: `exec`

Start a background service and read its state back to confirm it is running. When `scope` is omitted, checks "user" first and then "system" (`conflict` if in both). Changing a system service requires privileges: on Unix, legion never escalates unless `[svc] sudo = true` is set in node.toml (running `sudo -n`); on Windows the node must run elevated.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Service name to control. |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | `"user"` or `"system"`. When omitted, checks `"user"` first and then `"system"`. `user`: Per-user service manager (`systemctl --user` on Linux, `gui/<uid>` on macOS). `system`: Machine-wide service manager (the only scope on Windows). Allowed values: `user`, `system`. |

### `svc.status`

Effect: `read`

Read the current state, enabled flag, PID, start time, exit code and diagnostic properties of one background service. When `scope` is omitted, checks "user" first and then "system", returning which matched or `conflict` if the name exists in both. Read-only and never escalates privileges.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Service name (for example `nginx.service`, `com.example.worker` or `Spooler`). |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | `"user"` or `"system"`. When omitted, checks `"user"` first and then `"system"`. `user`: Per-user service manager (`systemctl --user` on Linux, `gui/<uid>` on macOS). `system`: Machine-wide service manager (the only scope on Windows). Allowed values: `user`, `system`. |

### `svc.stop`

Effect: `exec`

Stop a background service and read its state back to confirm it is stopped. When `scope` is omitted, checks "user" first and then "system" (`conflict` if in both). Changing a system service requires privileges: on Unix, legion never escalates unless `[svc] sudo = true` is set in node.toml (running `sudo -n`); on Windows the node must run elevated.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | Service name to control. |
| `scope` | `string` | no | - | `"user"` or `"system"`. When omitted, checks `"user"` first and then `"system"`. `user`: Per-user service manager (`systemctl --user` on Linux, `gui/<uid>` on macOS). `system`: Machine-wide service manager (the only scope on Windows). Allowed values: `user`, `system`. |

## sys

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sys.info` | `read` | Describe this machine: host name, operating system, uptime and boot id, CPU model, core count and current usage, memory and swap, disks, and NVIDIA GPUs. |
| `sys.kill` | `destroy` | Stop a process: ask it to exit, and force it after a short grace if it has not. |
| `sys.procs` | `read` | List the processes running on this machine, busiest first, with their id, parent, name, command line, user, CPU usage (percent of one core), memory in bytes and start time. |

### `sys.info`

Effect: `read`

Describe this machine: host name, operating system, uptime and boot id, CPU model, core count and current usage, memory and swap, disks, and NVIDIA GPUs. Sizes are bytes.

Takes no arguments.

### `sys.kill`

Effect: `destroy`

Stop a process: ask it to exit, and force it after a short grace if it has not. Pass the `start_time` sys.procs reported so a process that has since exited and whose id was reused is never hit. `tree` stops its descendants too; `force` skips asking.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pid` | `integer` | yes | - | The process id. Minimum: 0. |
| `start_time` | `string` | no | - | When the process started, as sys.procs reported it. When given and the process with this id started at another time, the id has been reused and nothing is stopped. |
| `tree` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Stop the process's descendants as well. |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Stop it at once instead of asking it to exit first. |

### `sys.procs`

Effect: `read`

List the processes running on this machine, busiest first, with their id, parent, name, command line, user, CPU usage (percent of one core), memory in bytes and start time. `filter` keeps those whose name or command line contains it. Command lines are shown with secret-looking values (passwords, tokens, credentials in URLs) replaced by [redacted].

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter` | `string` | no | - | Keep only processes whose name or command line contains this, ignoring case. |
| `sort` | `string` | no | - | What the busiest are measured by: `cpu` (the default) or `memory`. `cpu`: CPU usage, highest first. `memory`: Memory, largest first. Allowed values: `cpu`, `memory`. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no | - | How many processes to return, 1 to 500; 30 when absent. Minimum: 0. |

## token

| Tool | Effect | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token.add` | `admin` | Make a bearer token for `legion serve`, standing for one principal that policy.toml names and the caller could act as itself: its own, or any when the caller has the owner role. |
| `token.list` | `admin` | List the tokens `legion serve` accepts for principals the caller could act as: each one's name, principal, when it was made and when it expires. |
| `token.remove` | `admin` | Remove a token of a principal the caller could act as, so `legion serve` refuses it from its next request on and ends its MCP sessions. |

### `token.add`

Effect: `admin`

Make a bearer token for `legion serve`, standing for one principal that policy.toml names and the caller could act as itself: its own, or any when the caller has the owner role. The token is in this reply and nowhere else: only its hash is kept, so copy it now. A token for a principal with the owner role is the keys to the machine (whoever holds it may do anything the account can, from anywhere the server is published), so only a caller with the owner role may make one, and only with allow_owner true. A token made by a call that came with an expiring token expires no later.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | What to call the token, such as phone: lower-case letters, digits, - and _. |
| `principal` | `string` | yes | - | The principal every request with the token acts as. policy.toml must name it, which is what gives it a role. |
| `expires_days` | `integer` | no | - | Days until the token stops working; it never does when left out. Minimum: 0. |
| `allow_owner` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Allow a token for owner, which may do everything. Off unless given as true. |

### `token.list`

Effect: `admin`

List the tokens `legion serve` accepts for principals the caller could act as: each one's name, principal, when it was made and when it expires. The tokens themselves are not kept, so they cannot be shown.

Takes no arguments.

### `token.remove`

Effect: `admin`

Remove a token of a principal the caller could act as, so `legion serve` refuses it from its next request on and ends its MCP sessions.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | - | The token's name, as token.list shows it. |
